visibility_rules.public_message_on_enter: Someone leaves the hall, their footsteps fading into the corridor.

instructions: A player chooses a public location, receives a private environmental description, and must name an object to inspect. Never list object options. A correct hidden point grants its clue; an incorrect choice reveals nothing more.

locations.name: Crime Scene
locations.public_summary: The eastern guest chamber where King Duncan died. Blood and disturbed furnishings still bear the marks of last night.
locations.entry_narration: A dark trail of blood crosses the carpet toward the door. The fireplace ashes are still warm, and a metallic glint catches at their edge. A cup lies overturned beside the table, while a long cut splits the curtain.

result.message: You brush aside the warm ashes. A silver ring lies beneath them, engraved inside with the crest of Malcolm's personal guard.
The marks appear to come from the struggle. You find nothing more.
Only ordinary medicinal wine remains in the cup, likely Duncan's drink before sleep.
The damage seems to have been left by the struggle. You find nothing more.

locations.name: Macbeth's Room
locations.public_summary: Macbeth's private chamber, where a desk, a suit of armor, and a locked iron chest stand in uneasy silence.
locations.entry_narration: The Chronicles of Scotland lies open on the desk, its spine worn from use. Faint letters are carved inside the armor in the corner. A new lock secures the iron chest beneath the bed, and an unfinished family letter rests beneath an ink bottle.

result.message: A folded sheet is hidden between the pages: Macbeth's private letter to his wife.
The inscription is a common military mark recording the date of an old battle.
The chest contains military pay in silver. Nothing appears unusual.
It is an ordinary household letter asking that the evening feast be prepared.

locations.name: Malcolm's Room
locations.public_summary: The prince's temporary chamber. Maps of England and scattered papers give it the air of a war room.
locations.entry_narration: A dark green cloak lies neatly folded in a chest, though its lining feels unusually stiff. A crumpled parchment in the wastebasket bears the word 'Birnam.' A broken wax seal rests in the bedside drawer, and the map of England is creased from repeated use.

result.message: Inside the cloak's lining, you find a cloth-wrapped diary bearing Malcolm's name.
It is only a rejected withdrawal plan, written in anger.
The fragments are too damaged to reveal their origin.
It is a conventional campaign map marking the passes toward England.

locations.name: Banquo's Room
locations.public_summary: Banquo's chamber appears plain and orderly, though several details suggest that someone tried to hide a search.
locations.entry_narration: The room smells of lamp oil. One stone beside the bed stands slightly higher than the others, and no dust fills its edges. A metal box on the desk has a broken lock, scratches mark the edge of the wall map, and the lining of an old cloak has been opened and resewn.

result.message: A small metal box lies in the hollow beneath the stone. It holds Banquo's diary and an unsent secret letter.
Someone has already searched it. Only a few copper coins remain.
The markings correspond to defensive positions around the castle and appear to be military study.
It is only a poorly repaired garment, likely the work of an inexperienced servant.

locations.name: Macduff's Room
locations.public_summary: The Thane of Fife's chamber is austere, but a burned letter and a heavy candlestick appear out of place.
locations.entry_narration: The bronze candlestick is unusually heavy, and turning marks ring its base. A burned letter on the desk preserves part of the word 'alliance.' One petal of the stone iris carved into the fireplace can be pressed, while a faded family record beneath the bed bears a scratched reference to a Caesarean birth.

result.message: The base twists open to reveal a hollow compartment containing half of a parchment pact.
The letter is too badly burned; only scattered words remain legible.
A mechanism clicks behind the wall, but it opens only an abandoned passage.
It appears to be an ordinary genealogy. The note about birth may be no more than an old annotation.

ambient_locations.name: Lady Macbeth's Room
ambient_locations.description: The room smells of roses and iron. Candlelight trembles in a silver mirror, and a carved chest stands half-open near the bed.

ambient_locations.name: Cellar
ambient_locations.description: Wine barrels and herb shelves line damp stone walls. A bitter scent lingers in the air.

ambient_locations.name: Castle Corridor
ambient_locations.description: Stone walls stretch every footstep into an echo. The candles burn lower in the eastern gallery.

ambient_locations.name: Great Hall
ambient_locations.description: The long tables still bear traces of last night's feast, while the hearth has gone cold.

ambient_locations.name: Kitchen
ambient_locations.description: Warmth remains in the ovens, but the dishes have been washed and nothing unusual is visible.

ambient_locations.name: Servants' Quarters
ambient_locations.description: The narrow beds are neatly made. The servants avoid speaking of what happened last night.

ambient_locations.name: Courtyard
ambient_locations.description: Night dew darkens the stones, and the wind has scattered whatever footprints may once have remained.

ambient_location_rule.message: Provide only atmosphere and hints grounded in the script. Never invent evidence or issue a clue card here.
